title: Observation, Pattern, Context and Diagnostic Boundaries

publicSources.title: Overview of Plant Diagnostics
publicSources.scope: Transferable plant-diagnostic reasoning for host identity, site/history context, whole-plant inspection, symptoms/signs and pattern; not cannabis-specific and not a substitute for qualified diagnosis.

content.overview: A Technician I creates reliable evidence for diagnosis without pretending that every visible symptom proves a cause. This lesson trains learners to separate direct observations from interpretations, describe incidence and spatial pattern, add available environmental or work-history context, recognize urgent abnormalities, and escalate when the evidence or authority boundary does not support an independent conclusion.

vocabulary.definition: A description of directly visible, measured or otherwise documented evidence without an unsupported causal conclusion.
A reasoned meaning assigned to observations that may remain provisional until additional evidence confirms it.
The proportion or count of observed units showing a defined condition within the sampled population.
A set of plausible explanations considered when evidence does not yet support one confirmed cause.

sections.title: Describe before you diagnose
sections.body: Color change, tissue damage, posture, architecture, root appearance, developmental differences and spatial patterns can be recorded directly. A causal label such as nutrient deficiency, pathogen, irrigation failure or genetic weakness requires supporting evidence. Technician I records the observation and routes the case when diagnosis exceeds the task or available evidence.

sections.title: Pattern changes the investigation
sections.body: One plant, one bench, one irrigation zone, one room edge and an entire room represent different evidence patterns. Record counts or proportions where practical, location and severity using supplied definitions, and whether neighboring comparison plants show the same condition. Public extension diagnostic guidance likewise treats whole-plant distribution and site pattern as important clues rather than as stand-alone proof of cause.

sections.title: Context strengthens a note without proving cause
sections.body: Recent irrigation, environmental readings, lighting or equipment events, transplant or canopy work, IPM history and developmental stage can make an observation more useful. Diagnostic guidance emphasizes plant identity, site conditions and management history because different causes can produce similar symptoms. Context should therefore remain attached as evidence unless the supplied procedure and additional evidence justify a confirmed conclusion.

sections.title: Interpretation is a hypothesis layer
sections.body: A strong interpretation narrows possibilities and identifies what evidence would distinguish them; it does not erase uncertainty. When multiple causes remain plausible, preserve the differential and the missing evidence rather than converting the most familiar explanation into a fact.

sections.title: Escalate consequence and uncertainty
sections.body: Sudden widespread wilt, suspected spreading pest or disease evidence, unexpected reproductive morphology, strong root-zone abnormality, substantial zone differences or damage associated with equipment or work can require prompt escalation. Follow the supplied procedure and preserve the original condition before changing it when safe to do so.

workedExamples: Older lower leaves on 6 of 20 sampled plants in Zone B show interveinal yellowing. The note records distribution, location, photos and available root-zone measurements without declaring a specific deficiency.

A room-wide droop appears shortly after a scheduled irrigation event. The technician records the timing and pattern, checks supplied irrigation and environmental status, and escalates rather than independently changing the control strategy.
commonMistakes: Replacing an objective description with a disease or nutrient label that has not been verified.
Recording an environmental or irrigation event as proof of cause rather than as context.
Treating one spatial pattern as uniquely diagnostic when multiple explanations remain possible.
Changing conditions before documenting the original abnormal state when there is no immediate safety reason to do so.
content.practicalApplication: Sort a set of crop notes into direct observation, pattern, context, interpretation and unsupported diagnosis. Rewrite weak notes to include location, distribution, developmental context, uncertainty and escalation status, then identify what additional evidence would be needed before a stronger conclusion could be supported.
content.summary: Technician I observation protects the distinction between evidence and diagnosis. Strong notes preserve what changed, where, how widely, under what context, what remains uncertain and what was escalated, allowing a qualified person to investigate without inheriting an unsupported conclusion.

blocks.title: Observation, interpretation, and diagnostic-boundary workflow
blocks.alt: Four-stage diagram moving from direct observation to spatial pattern and context, then provisional interpretation, and finally confirmation or escalation, with reminders that symptoms, timing and context can narrow possibilities without proving a single cause.
blocks.caption: Build the evidence chain before naming a cause: observe first, preserve pattern and context, keep interpretation provisional, then confirm or escalate according to the available evidence and role.

blocks.title: A clue is not proof
blocks.body: Plant diagnostic guidance uses host identity, symptoms/signs, distribution, site conditions and history together because different problems can look similar. Treat each clue as evidence that changes the differential—not as automatic confirmation of one cause.

blocks.title: One zone droops after irrigation
blocks.setting: Plants in one irrigation zone are drooping while the rest of the room remains upright. A scheduled irrigation event just completed.
blocks.prompt: What is the strongest Technician I response?
options: Record irrigation failure as confirmed and reprogram the controller
Record the zone pattern, compare representative points, check supplied irrigation/environment status and escalate unresolved deviation
Water the entire room again because droop always means drought
Delete the observation if plants may recover later
blocks.answer: Record the zone pattern, compare representative points, check supplied irrigation/environment status and escalate unresolved deviation
blocks.feedback: The spatial pattern and timing are useful evidence, but neither proves the cause or authorizes independent control redesign.
